subject: Private Offer: staggered signature windows and license model alignment for co-sell
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@finvelope.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finvelope.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private Offer: staggered signature windows and license model alignment for co-sell

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has a couple of questions before we can sign the AWS Private Offer:

- We have two legal entities (Finvelope US and Finvelope EU). Can signatures be staged so one entity signs first and the other follows within a 30-day window?
- We prefer to align the license model to our usage tiers (dev/staging/prod) rather than flat seat counts — will that require a custom amendment to the PO?
- Any constraints from the AWS Private Offer flow that would block staged signatures or staggered effective dates?

Cc'ing procurement so they have visibility. We need to confirm this before our board sign-off next week.

Best,
Sara Patel
VP Product, Finvelope
[sara.patel@finvelope.com]

[Attachment: Finvelope_requirements_v1.docx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@finvelope.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, procurement@finvelope.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer: staggered signature windows and license model alignment for co-sell

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a staged signature window and we can map the PO to a tiered license model; there are just a few sequencing steps for the AWS Private Offer flow.

High-level approach (proposal):
- Staged signatures: Create a single Private Offer with the total committed value but include a contract addendum we control that allows staged execution by entity. The buyer's first signature executes the offer; the second signature for the EU entity can be recorded as an addendum acceptance within a 30-day window. AWS allows this so long as the Marketplace order references the same Private Offer ID.
- License mapping: We propose an appendix that maps AWS metering lines to your dev/staging/prod tiers. That appendix lives outside the Marketplace listing (in the SOW) and we reconcile usage monthly.
- Risk points: The buyer must ensure both signatures are from authorized signers and that billing account mapping in AWS matches the entity that will be charged. If billing needs to be split across AWS accounts, we need to coordinate with Kyle (AWS partner).

I attached a draft SOW and a license-mapping spreadsheet for review. If that looks good I can prepare the DocuSign packet and a short runbook for AWS Private Offer submission.

Next steps:
1) Confirm you want the 30-day staging window (can be 14/30/60).
2) Confirm whether billing will be consolidated to one AWS account or split by entity.
3) Approve attached SOW for DocuSign prep.

Thanks — I can hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Marketplace GTM, Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.com]

[Attachments: RWI-Finvelope_SOW_v3.pdf, license-mapping-table.xlsx]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer: staggered signature windows and license model alignment for co-sell

Heads up — internal note before we finalize language with Finvelope: 

- For AWS compliance, we must keep the Private Offer ID constant. Any commercial carve-outs should be captured in the SOW/Appendix, not in the Marketplace listing itself.
- If Finvelope wants split billing across two AWS accounts, that introduces extra ops steps and likely delays (AWS needs account linkage). If they consolidate billing but allocate internally via their own chargebacks, that's fastest.
- Co-sell credits: remind Finvelope that co-sell incentives depend on the AWS seller account mapping; loop Kyle early.

I'll review the SOW appendix and send suggested clause language for staged execution (short clause for DocuSign).

- Vanessa

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@finvelope.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finvelope.com, Kyle Brooks <kyle.brooks@aws-partner.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer: staggered signature windows and license model alignment for co-sell

Thanks Karthik — that approach sounds reasonable. A couple clarifications from procurement: 

- We want a 30-day window between signatures — legal is okay with that if the SOW clearly states effective date and billing start.
- We prefer billing consolidated to Finvelope US for now (single AWS payer account). Can you confirm that we won't lose any co-sell benefits under consolidated billing? Kyle, can you confirm?
- Procurement requests a buyer signatory matrix showing who signs which entity and the order of signatures. Can you supply that?

If you can share the DocuSign packet and the signatory matrix by Monday, we can route for internal approval.

Best,
Sara

Sara — great, thanks for confirming the 30-day window and consolidated billing. Below is the signatory sequencing and delivery plan we'll execute this week.

1) Documents delivered (today):
   - DocuSign packet created: Private Offer acceptance + SOW appendix + license mapping table.
   - Static files uploaded to HubSpot under the deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/RWI-2026-FIN-289

2) Signatory sequencing (order of execution):
   - Step A: Finvelope US (primary AWS payer) signs the Private Offer acceptance and SOW. This executes the Marketplace order and starts the billing reference.
   - Step B: Finvelope EU signs the SOW addendum within 30 days; the addendum references the same Private Offer ID and confirms EU entity's operational acceptance (no new Marketplace order required).

3) Billing and co-sell mapping:
   - Consolidated billing to Finvelope US is supported. Kyle please confirm that co-sell attribution will be preserved under the consolidated payer mapping (CC'd).
   - We will include an appendix row mapping your "dev/staging/prod" tiers to the AWS metering lines so usage reconciliation is straightforward.

4) Ops notes and AWS constraints:
   - AWS requires the Marketplace order to reference the same offer ID. The SOW addendum must explicitly tie to that ID.
   - If Finvelope later requests split billing across AWS accounts, we'll need to reopen the private offer and coordinate account linkage with AWS — expect a 2-3 week window for that work.

5) Next actions for Finvelope (requested by Tue EOD):
   - Signatory matrix spreadsheet (who signs what and order) — template attached.
   - Confirm DocuSign signers and emails.
   - Final approval of SOW appendix.
